title: Chess Run Analysis
h1: Chess in Salesforce: how the prompts and the model did
lede: Grok 4.7 at medium effort built a chess rules engine in Apex with a Lightning board in the owner's Developer Edition org, on ShipLoop 1.5.0 plus the first efficiency wave. The run ended blocked at release-verify waiting for six itemized board observations. Every prompt ShipLoop wrote is below with the model's reasoning, words, tool calls and outputs, its result, the earlier packet review's scores, and each Improve review, judged against three questions. Many of the fixes it led to are already in the Battleship run.
figures: at release-verify after 26 accepted stages; the app works and is kept

step_by_step.label: No
step_by_step.text: Step-plan cut three steps (engine, controller, board), but the only check row was S3's board grep and ShipLoop ran every check after every step, so S1 could not finish. The step-plan Improve review, not implement, then merged all three into one step; it saw the right fix (a regression test) but guessed the gate would reject it. One 17-minute implement built all 11 files and one review covered the whole item. Fixed since: each step now has its own proof and runs only that.

improve.label: Mixed
improve.text: Planning reviews found real oracle defects that held through the org tests (FEN fields, castling, deploy-then-TAP). They also passed an impossible promotion line and missed the tab-visibility prerequisite, both of which reached the owner; the implement review found the AuraHandledException message issue and then talked itself out of it, and verify had to fix it. Of the outer-stage reviews, 1 in 4 found something real.

directive.label: Weak where gates lived in code
directive.text: Where the stage method was in the packet the model read nothing else (research, spec, release). Where a rule lived only in ShipLoop's code the model read the code: 26 times in preparation and 109 times in the release half, 34 of them at release-plan to learn the delivery contract. Release-verify had no rule for a partial person reply and blocked twice.
